subject.title: Feature: fallbackChannel for hook mappings when primary delivery fails

question: Should hook mappings gain a public ordered fallback delivery config, and what exact retry semantics should apply after a primary channel send fails?
rationale: This adds new public configuration and cross-channel fallback behavior, and OpenClaw policy treats fallback behavior plus config surface additions as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Add typed hook fallback chain
options.body: Approve a narrow `fallbackChannels` contract for explicit user-configured alternates, with docs and tests for retry ordering, delivery status, and all-targets-failed reporting.

options.title: Keep failure notifications separate
options.body: Do not add hook result failover now; document that `failureDestination` covers failed-run notifications, while hook result delivery remains single-target.

options.title: Fold into broad delivery contract
options.body: Defer this request into the broader durable final delivery semantics work, accepting slower resolution for the Gmail-style hook fallback use case.

recommendation.title: Add typed hook fallback chain
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow `fallbackChannels` contract for explicit user-configured alternates, with docs and tests for retry ordering, delivery status, and all-targets-failed reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has the strongest available hook mapping feature-history signal.
